# gh-994: validation_failed label not auto-cleared on head change (park-reset broken) — operator hit it 4x today

## Description

## Goal — validation_failed park state becomes a pure function of the CURRENT head (v2, full reframe per create-goal discipline)

One sentence: **the `validation_failed` label on a PR always and only reflects the check state of the PR's current head** — any head change resets the park automatically, so no PR can ever sit "parked" on a failure that belongs to a superseded commit.

Today the label is sticky across head changes: after a kicker push / rework push / operator push moves the head, the label set for the OLD head is not removed, the SM keeps treating the PR as parked, the validation arm never re-arms, and the queue stalls until a human deletes the label. On 2026-10-17 alone this required 4 manual interventions (3× on fa #1563, 1× on fa #1566) — each one papering over the same defect.

## Why this framing

- **Retracted:** "operator clears stale validation_failed labels" (done 4× on 2026-10-17). Owner directive: manual clearing masks the bug; the pipeline must self-reset. This card fixes the machine, not the symptom.
- **Retracted:** "the SM re-arms on label removal" as the designed reset path. The designed reset is the *head-change event*, per the machine's own published comment contract on parked PRs: *"Your push clears the validation_failed park via the head-change reset."* The contract exists; the implementation is what is broken.

## Architecture

Named lifecycle of the park state (subject of every verb is explicit — the OBJECT being mutated is the **PR's label set**, keyed to a **head SHA**):

```
push event (kicker / rework leg / operator / merge-main)
        │
        ▼
[head-change detector] ──reads──▶ PR.headRefOid (BEFORE vs AFTER)
        │ heads differ
        ▼
[park reset] ──removes──▶ label validation_failed  (only if present)
        │                       │
        │                       └── invariant: label removal is unconditional
        │                           on head change — never re-checks old state
        ▼
[arm gate] ──sees──▶ no park label → PR eligible for validation arm
```

**Invariants (asserted by tests, not prose):**
- **I1** — For every PR, `labelPresent(validation_failed)` ⟹ the label's recorded head SHA == current `headRefOid`. Any mismatch is unreachable state; the reset makes it impossible, not merely unlikely.
- **I2** — The reset fires for EVERY head-mutation source: kicker push, machine rework push, operator push, silent merge-main branch update by the merge bot. No source may bypass the detector.
- **I3** — Reset and removal are idempotent and race-safe: N concurrent head-change events produce exactly ≤1 label removal and never a re-add.
- **I4** — The published comment contract stays true verbatim: any push that changes the head clears the park; no comment edit needed (the contract was right, the code was wrong).

## Capability surface (every head-mutation source → reset obligation)

| Head-mutation source | Resets park today? | Must reset (this card) |
|---|---|---|
| 🥁 kicker push (armed validation refresh) | **NO** (observed: fa #1566, kicker 18:09Z, label persisted 20+ min) | YES — core |
| Machine rework-leg push (fix commit) | unknown, assumed NO (same code path gap) | YES — core |
| Operator push to PR branch | NO (fa #1563 cycle, 3×) | YES — core |
| Merge-bot silent merge-main branch update | unknown | YES — core |
| PR reopened / retargeted | NO (not observed, same class) | YES — second tier |

**Tiered inventory:**
- **Core (this card):** I1–I4 for all four core sources; reset removes the label and leaves an audit trail entry (machine log line `park-reset: <pr> head <old>→<new>`).
- **Second tier (opt-in follow-up):** reset also *re-dispatches* validation automatically for armed-eligible PRs (today a separate SM turn does this — fine to keep).
- **Excluded (rationale):** resetting on *check-run completion* events — completion is not a head change and would fight the label's purpose (the label is the park); excluded deliberately.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — Unit: given a PR carrying `validation_failed` with recorded head `H1`, when the head-change detector observes `headRefOid` becoming `H2 ≠ H1`, the reset removes the label. *Hook: park-state unit test over the detector with injected head refs.*
- **AC2** — Integration (fake GitHub): each of the four core sources produces a head change → exactly one label removal follows within the same SM/merge-bot turn; no removal occurs when head is unchanged. *Hook: scripted scenario runner with recorded API fixtures.*
- **AC3** — Contract: the detector compares full SHAs (not prefixes, not branch names) and treats force-push (same branch, new SHA) identically to fast-forward. *Hook: AC2 variant with force-push fixture.*
- **AC4** — Race: two concurrent pushes (kicker + operator) → ≤1 removal, no error, no re-add. *Hook: concurrent-event fixture.*
- **AC5** — Regression (live-shape): replay the fa #1566 timeline (label set on `H1`, kicker push to `bf0828c4`, all checks green) → label absent at end of the kicker's own run. *Hook: E2E scenario keyed to the recorded run ids (39054011685).*

## Test plan

### Test matrix
- `UT-1..3` — pure state machine of the park lifecycle (set/park/reset), no IO. Maps AC1, AC3, AC4.
- `IT-1..4` — fake-API scenarios, one per head-mutation source. Maps AC2.
- `E2E-1` — real repo sandbox: push red → label set → push green head → label gone without any human call. Maps AC5.
- `REG-1` — fa queue simulation: 5 PRs parked on stale labels under the old behavior replayed against the new code; assert none remain parked after one SM pass. **CI rule: a red REG job blocks merge of this fix even when UT/IT/E2E are all green** (this is exactly the class of bug that only shows up in queue shape).

### Edge / border cases
- **E1** — Head changes while a validation run for the OLD head is still in flight: old run's result must never re-set the park for the new head (result is keyed to the SHA it ran on).
- **E2** — Push that keeps the tree identical (empty amend, re-tag): SHA changes anyway → reset fires (correct: a new SHA is a new claim of "look again").
- **E3** — Label manually re-added between head change and SM turn: the reset has fired already; the label now records the NEW head and behaves as a fresh park (no hidden unbounded loops).
- **E4** — GitHub API failure mid-reset: retry with backoff; the SM turn must not crash; worst case the label survives ONE extra turn (degradation path, not a stall).
- **E5** — PR closed while parked: label irrelevant; no reset needed; no crash on later events.

## Non-goals

- Changing WHAT counts as red (check-selection logic is untouched).
- Auto-dispatching validation on reset (second tier; the existing arm gate handles it).
- Touching `rework-loop-escalated` / `blocked` / `validation_failed`-on-current-head semantics — those are separate state machines (see agents#990 for the escalation one).
- Manual label-clearing runbooks — permanently retired; any future human clear of this label is a bug report, not a procedure.

## Open questions

- **Q1** — Where does the fix land: the shared dma/SM scripts in dmtools-agents (both repos' legs resolve `latest`) or fa-specific config? *Default assumption: agents repo, shared path, since the contract text ships from there.*
- **Q2** — Should the reset emit the audit comment on the PR (visible trail for operators) or only a machine-log line? *Default: machine-log line only; PR comments on automated housekeeping became noise today.*

- Live instances 2026-10-17: fa #1563 (3×), fa #1566 (kicker push run 39054011685, head `bf0828c4`).
- Precedent for machine-bug-fix flow: dmtools-agents#969 (rework retry loop fix shipped through the same pipeline).
- Sibling defect (same family, separate card): dmtools-agents#990 — rework-loop-escalated false positive also jams the validate-armed pointer.
- The contract sentence being violated, quoted from the machine's own parked-PR comment: *"Your push clears the validation_failed park via the head-change reset."*

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write

# gh-994: validation_failed label not auto-cleared on head change (park-reset broken) — operator hit it 4x today

## Description

## Goal — validation_failed park state becomes a pure function of the CURRENT head (v2, full reframe per create-goal discipline)

One sentence: **the `validation_failed` label on a PR always and only reflects the check state of the PR's current head** — any head change resets the park automatically, so no PR can ever sit "parked" on a failure that belongs to a superseded commit.

Today the label is sticky across head changes: after a kicker push / rework push / operator push moves the head, the label set for the OLD head is not removed, the SM keeps treating the PR as parked, the validation arm never re-arms, and the queue stalls until a human deletes the label. On 2026-10-17 alone this required 4 manual interventions (3× on fa #1563, 1× on fa #1566) — each one papering over the same defect.

## Why this framing

- **Retracted:** "operator clears stale validation_failed labels" (done 4× on 2026-10-17). Owner directive: manual clearing masks the bug; the pipeline must self-reset. This card fixes the machine, not the symptom.
- **Retracted:** "the SM re-arms on label removal" as the designed reset path. The designed reset is the *head-change event*, per the machine's own published comment contract on parked PRs: *"Your push clears the validation_failed park via the head-change reset."* The contract exists; the implementation is what is broken.

## Architecture

Named lifecycle of the park state (subject of every verb is explicit — the OBJECT being mutated is the **PR's label set**, keyed to a **head SHA**):

```
push event (kicker / rework leg / operator / merge-main)
        │
        ▼
[head-change detector] ──reads──▶ PR.headRefOid (BEFORE vs AFTER)
        │ heads differ
        ▼
[park reset] ──removes──▶ label validation_failed  (only if present)
        │                       │
        │                       └── invariant: label removal is unconditional
        │                           on head change — never re-checks old state
        ▼
[arm gate] ──sees──▶ no park label → PR eligible for validation arm
```

**Invariants (asserted by tests, not prose):**
- **I1** — For every PR, `labelPresent(validation_failed)` ⟹ the label's recorded head SHA == current `headRefOid`. Any mismatch is unreachable state; the reset makes it impossible, not merely unlikely.
- **I2** — The reset fires for EVERY head-mutation source: kicker push, machine rework push, operator push, silent merge-main branch update by the merge bot. No source may bypass the detector.
- **I3** — Reset and removal are idempotent and race-safe: N concurrent head-change events produce exactly ≤1 label removal and never a re-add.
- **I4** — The published comment contract stays true verbatim: any push that changes the head clears the park; no comment edit needed (the contract was right, the code was wrong).

## Capability surface (every head-mutation source → reset obligation)

| Head-mutation source | Resets park today? | Must reset (this card) |
|---|---|---|
| 🥁 kicker push (armed validation refresh) | **NO** (observed: fa #1566, kicker 18:09Z, label persisted 20+ min) | YES — core |
| Machine rework-leg push (fix commit) | unknown, assumed NO (same code path gap) | YES — core |
| Operator push to PR branch | NO (fa #1563 cycle, 3×) | YES — core |
| Merge-bot silent merge-main branch update | unknown | YES — core |
| PR reopened / retargeted | NO (not observed, same class) | YES — second tier |

**Tiered inventory:**
- **Core (this card):** I1–I4 for all four core sources; reset removes the label and leaves an audit trail entry (machine log line `park-reset: <pr> head <old>→<new>`).
- **Second tier (opt-in follow-up):** reset also *re-dispatches* validation automatically for armed-eligible PRs (today a separate SM turn does this — fine to keep).
- **Excluded (rationale):** resetting on *check-run completion* events — completion is not a head change and would fight the label's purpose (the label is the park); excluded deliberately.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — Unit: given a PR carrying `validation_failed` with recorded head `H1`, when the head-change detector observes `headRefOid` becoming `H2 ≠ H1`, the reset removes the label. *Hook: park-state unit test over the detector with injected head refs.*
- **AC2** — Integration (fake GitHub): each of the four core sources produces a head change → exactly one label removal follows within the same SM/merge-bot turn; no removal occurs when head is unchanged. *Hook: scripted scenario runner with recorded API fixtures.*
- **AC3** — Contract: the detector compares full SHAs (not prefixes, not branch names) and treats force-push (same branch, new SHA) identically to fast-forward. *Hook: AC2 variant with force-push fixture.*
- **AC4** — Race: two concurrent pushes (kicker + operator) → ≤1 removal, no error, no re-add. *Hook: concurrent-event fixture.*
- **AC5** — Regression (live-shape): replay the fa #1566 timeline (label set on `H1`, kicker push to `bf0828c4`, all checks green) → label absent at end of the kicker's own run. *Hook: E2E scenario keyed to the recorded run ids (39054011685).*

## Test plan

### Test matrix
- `UT-1..3` — pure state machine of the park lifecycle (set/park/reset), no IO. Maps AC1, AC3, AC4.
- `IT-1..4` — fake-API scenarios, one per head-mutation source. Maps AC2.
- `E2E-1` — real repo sandbox: push red → label set → push green head → label gone without any human call. Maps AC5.
- `REG-1` — fa queue simulation: 5 PRs parked on stale labels under the old behavior replayed against the new code; assert none remain parked after one SM pass. **CI rule: a red REG job blocks merge of this fix even when UT/IT/E2E are all green** (this is exactly the class of bug that only shows up in queue shape).

### Edge / border cases
- **E1** — Head changes while a validation run for the OLD head is still in flight: old run's result must never re-set the park for the new head (result is keyed to the SHA it ran on).
- **E2** — Push that keeps the tree identical (empty amend, re-tag): SHA changes anyway → reset fires (correct: a new SHA is a new claim of "look again").
- **E3** — Label manually re-added between head change and SM turn: the reset has fired already; the label now records the NEW head and behaves as a fresh park (no hidden unbounded loops).
- **E4** — GitHub API failure mid-reset: retry with backoff; the SM turn must not crash; worst case the label survives ONE extra turn (degradation path, not a stall).
- **E5** — PR closed while parked: label irrelevant; no reset needed; no crash on later events.

## Non-goals

- Changing WHAT counts as red (check-selection logic is untouched).
- Auto-dispatching validation on reset (second tier; the existing arm gate handles it).
- Touching `rework-loop-escalated` / `blocked` / `validation_failed`-on-current-head semantics — those are separate state machines (see agents#990 for the escalation one).
- Manual label-clearing runbooks — permanently retired; any future human clear of this label is a bug report, not a procedure.

## Open questions

- **Q1** — Where does the fix land: the shared dma/SM scripts in dmtools-agents (both repos' legs resolve `latest`) or fa-specific config? *Default assumption: agents repo, shared path, since the contract text ships from there.*
- **Q2** — Should the reset emit the audit comment on the PR (visible trail for operators) or only a machine-log line? *Default: machine-log line only; PR comments on automated housekeeping became noise today.*

- Sibling defect (same family, separate card): dmtools-agents#990 — rework-loop-escalated false positive also jams the validate-armed pointer.
- The contract sentence being violated, quoted from the machine's own parked-PR comment: *"Your push clears the validation_failed park via the head-change reset."*

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write

# gh-994: validation_failed label not auto-cleared on head change (park-reset broken) — operator hit it 4x today

## Description

## Goal — validation_failed park state becomes a pure function of the CURRENT head (v2, full reframe per create-goal discipline)

One sentence: **the `validation_failed` label on a PR always and only reflects the check state of the PR's current head** — any head change resets the park automatically, so no PR can ever sit "parked" on a failure that belongs to a superseded commit.

Today the label is sticky across head changes: after a kicker push / rework push / operator push moves the head, the label set for the OLD head is not removed, the SM keeps treating the PR as parked, the validation arm never re-arms, and the queue stalls until a human deletes the label. On 2026-10-17 alone this required 4 manual interventions (3× on fa #1563, 1× on fa #1566) — each one papering over the same defect.

## Why this framing

- **Retracted:** "operator clears stale validation_failed labels" (done 4× on 2026-10-17). Owner directive: manual clearing masks the bug; the pipeline must self-reset. This card fixes the machine, not the symptom.
- **Retracted:** "the SM re-arms on label removal" as the designed reset path. The designed reset is the *head-change event*, per the machine's own published comment contract on parked PRs: *"Your push clears the validation_failed park via the head-change reset."* The contract exists; the implementation is what is broken.

## Architecture

Named lifecycle of the park state (subject of every verb is explicit — the OBJECT being mutated is the **PR's label set**, keyed to a **head SHA**):

```
push event (kicker / rework leg / operator / merge-main)
        │
        ▼
[head-change detector] ──reads──▶ PR.headRefOid (BEFORE vs AFTER)
        │ heads differ
        ▼
[park reset] ──removes──▶ label validation_failed  (only if present)
        │                       │
        │                       └── invariant: label removal is unconditional
        │                           on head change — never re-checks old state
        ▼
[arm gate] ──sees──▶ no park label → PR eligible for validation arm
```

**Invariants (asserted by tests, not prose):**
- **I1** — For every PR, `labelPresent(validation_failed)` ⟹ the label's recorded head SHA == current `headRefOid`. Any mismatch is unreachable state; the reset makes it impossible, not merely unlikely.
- **I2** — The reset fires for EVERY head-mutation source: kicker push, machine rework push, operator push, silent merge-main branch update by the merge bot. No source may bypass the detector.
- **I3** — Reset and removal are idempotent and race-safe: N concurrent head-change events produce exactly ≤1 label removal and never a re-add.
- **I4** — The published comment contract stays true verbatim: any push that changes the head clears the park; no comment edit needed (the contract was right, the code was wrong).

## Capability surface (every head-mutation source → reset obligation)

| Head-mutation source | Resets park today? | Must reset (this card) |
|---|---|---|
| 🥁 kicker push (armed validation refresh) | **NO** (observed: fa #1566, kicker 18:09Z, label persisted 20+ min) | YES — core |
| Machine rework-leg push (fix commit) | unknown, assumed NO (same code path gap) | YES — core |
| Operator push to PR branch | NO (fa #1563 cycle, 3×) | YES — core |
| Merge-bot silent merge-main branch update | unknown | YES — core |
| PR reopened / retargeted | NO (not observed, same class) | YES — second tier |

**Tiered inventory:**
- **Core (this card):** I1–I4 for all four core sources; reset removes the label and leaves an audit trail entry (machine log line `park-reset: <pr> head <old>→<new>`).
- **Second tier (opt-in follow-up):** reset also *re-dispatches* validation automatically for armed-eligible PRs (today a separate SM turn does this — fine to keep).
- **Excluded (rationale):** resetting on *check-run completion* events — completion is not a head change and would fight the label's purpose (the label is the park); excluded deliberately.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — Unit: given a PR carrying `validation_failed` with recorded head `H1`, when the head-change detector observes `headRefOid` becoming `H2 ≠ H1`, the reset removes the label. *Hook: park-state unit test over the detector with injected head refs.*
- **AC2** — Integration (fake GitHub): each of the four core sources produces a head change → exactly one label removal follows within the same SM/merge-bot turn; no removal occurs when head is unchanged. *Hook: scripted scenario runner with recorded API fixtures.*
- **AC3** — Contract: the detector compares full SHAs (not prefixes, not branch names) and treats force-push (same branch, new SHA) identically to fast-forward. *Hook: AC2 variant with force-push fixture.*
- **AC4** — Race: two concurrent pushes (kicker + operator) → ≤1 removal, no error, no re-add. *Hook: concurrent-event fixture.*
- **AC5** — Regression (live-shape): replay the fa #1566 timeline (label set on `H1`, kicker push to `bf0828c4`, all checks green) → label absent at end of the kicker's own run. *Hook: E2E scenario keyed to the recorded run ids (39054011685).*

## Test plan

### Test matrix
- `UT-1..3` — pure state machine of the park lifecycle (set/park/reset), no IO. Maps AC1, AC3, AC4.
- `IT-1..4` — fake-API scenarios, one per head-mutation source. Maps AC2.
- `E2E-1` — real repo sandbox: push red → label set → push green head → label gone without any human call. Maps AC5.
- `REG-1` — fa queue simulation: 5 PRs parked on stale labels under the old behavior replayed against the new code; assert none remain parked after one SM pass. **CI rule: a red REG job blocks merge of this fix even when UT/IT/E2E are all green** (this is exactly the class of bug that only shows up in queue shape).

### Edge / border cases
- **E1** — Head changes while a validation run for the OLD head is still in flight: old run's result must never re-set the park for the new head (result is keyed to the SHA it ran on).
- **E2** — Push that keeps the tree identical (empty amend, re-tag): SHA changes anyway → reset fires (correct: a new SHA is a new claim of "look again").
- **E3** — Label manually re-added between head change and SM turn: the reset has fired already; the label now records the NEW head and behaves as a fresh park (no hidden unbounded loops).
- **E4** — GitHub API failure mid-reset: retry with backoff; the SM turn must not crash; worst case the label survives ONE extra turn (degradation path, not a stall).
- **E5** — PR closed while parked: label irrelevant; no reset needed; no crash on later events.

## Non-goals

- Changing WHAT counts as red (check-selection logic is untouched).
- Auto-dispatching validation on reset (second tier; the existing arm gate handles it).
- Touching `rework-loop-escalated` / `blocked` / `validation_failed`-on-current-head semantics — those are separate state machines (see agents#990 for the escalation one).
- Manual label-clearing runbooks — permanently retired; any future human clear of this label is a bug report, not a procedure.

## Open questions

- **Q1** — Where does the fix land: the shared dma/SM scripts in dmtools-agents (both repos' legs resolve `latest`) or fa-specific config? *Default assumption: agents repo, shared path, since the contract text ships from there.*
- **Q2** — Should the reset emit the audit comment on the PR (visible trail for operators) or only a machine-log line? *Default: machine-log line only; PR comments on automated housekeeping became noise today.*

- Live instances 2026-10-17: fa #1563 (3×), fa #1566 (kicker push run 39054011685, head `bf0828c4`).
- Precedent for machine-bug-fix flow: dmtools-agents#969 (rework retry loop fix shipped through the same pipeline).
- Sibling defect (same family, separate card): dmtools-agents#990 — rework-loop-escalated false positive also jams the validate-armed pointer.
- The contract sentence being violated, quoted from the machine's own parked-PR comment: *"Your push clears the validation_failed park via the head-change reset."*

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write

# gh-994: validation_failed label not auto-cleared on head change (park-reset broken) — operator hit it 4x today

## Description

## Goal — validation_failed park state becomes a pure function of the CURRENT head (v2, full reframe per create-goal discipline)

One sentence: **the `validation_failed` label on a PR always and only reflects the check state of the PR's current head** — any head change resets the park automatically, so no PR can ever sit "parked" on a failure that belongs to a superseded commit.

Today the label is sticky across head changes: after a kicker push / rework push / operator push moves the head, the label set for the OLD head is not removed, the SM keeps treating the PR as parked, the validation arm never re-arms, and the queue stalls until a human deletes the label. On 2026-10-17 alone this required 4 manual interventions (3× on fa #1563, 1× on fa #1566) — each one papering over the same defect.

## Why this framing

- **Retracted:** "operator clears stale validation_failed labels" (done 4× on 2026-10-17). Owner directive: manual clearing masks the bug; the pipeline must self-reset. This card fixes the machine, not the symptom.
- **Retracted:** "the SM re-arms on label removal" as the designed reset path. The designed reset is the *head-change event*, per the machine's own published comment contract on parked PRs: *"Your push clears the validation_failed park via the head-change reset."* The contract exists; the implementation is what is broken.

## Architecture

Named lifecycle of the park state (subject of every verb is explicit — the OBJECT being mutated is the **PR's label set**, keyed to a **head SHA**):

```
push event (kicker / rework leg / operator / merge-main)
        │
        ▼
[head-change detector] ──reads──▶ PR.headRefOid (BEFORE vs AFTER)
        │ heads differ
        ▼
[park reset] ──removes──▶ label validation_failed  (only if present)
        │                       │
        │                       └── invariant: label removal is unconditional
        │                           on head change — never re-checks old state
        ▼
[arm gate] ──sees──▶ no park label → PR eligible for validation arm
```

**Invariants (asserted by tests, not prose):**
- **I1** — For every PR, `labelPresent(validation_failed)` ⟹ the label's recorded head SHA == current `headRefOid`. Any mismatch is unreachable state; the reset makes it impossible, not merely unlikely.
- **I2** — The reset fires for EVERY head-mutation source: kicker push, machine rework push, operator push, silent merge-main branch update by the merge bot. No source may bypass the detector.
- **I3** — Reset and removal are idempotent and race-safe: N concurrent head-change events produce exactly ≤1 label removal and never a re-add.
- **I4** — The published comment contract stays true verbatim: any push that changes the head clears the park; no comment edit needed (the contract was right, the code was wrong).

## Capability surface (every head-mutation source → reset obligation)

| Head-mutation source | Resets park today? | Must reset (this card) |
|---|---|---|
| 🥁 kicker push (armed validation refresh) | **NO** (observed: fa #1566, kicker 18:09Z, label persisted 20+ min) | YES — core |
| Machine rework-leg push (fix commit) | unknown, assumed NO (same code path gap) | YES — core |
| Operator push to PR branch | NO (fa #1563 cycle, 3×) | YES — core |
| Merge-bot silent merge-main branch update | unknown | YES — core |
| PR reopened / retargeted | NO (not observed, same class) | YES — second tier |

**Tiered inventory:**
- **Core (this card):** I1–I4 for all four core sources; reset removes the label and leaves an audit trail entry (machine log line `park-reset: <pr> head <old>→<new>`).
- **Second tier (opt-in follow-up):** reset also *re-dispatches* validation automatically for armed-eligible PRs (today a separate SM turn does this — fine to keep).
- **Excluded (rationale):** resetting on *check-run completion* events — completion is not a head change and would fight the label's purpose (the label is the park); excluded deliberately.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — Unit: given a PR carrying `validation_failed` with recorded head `H1`, when the head-change detector observes `headRefOid` becoming `H2 ≠ H1`, the reset removes the label. *Hook: park-state unit test over the detector with injected head refs.*
- **AC2** — Integration (fake GitHub): each of the four core sources produces a head change → exactly one label removal follows within the same SM/merge-bot turn; no removal occurs when head is unchanged. *Hook: scripted scenario runner with recorded API fixtures.*

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write

# gh-994: validation_failed label not auto-cleared on head change (park-reset broken) — operator hit it 4x today

## Description

## Goal — validation_failed park state becomes a pure function of the CURRENT head (v2, full reframe per create-goal discipline)

One sentence: **the `validation_failed` label on a PR always and only reflects the check state of the PR's current head** — any head change resets the park automatically, so no PR can ever sit "parked" on a failure that belongs to a superseded commit.

Today the label is sticky across head changes: after a kicker push / rework push / operator push moves the head, the label set for the OLD head is not removed, the SM keeps treating the PR as parked, the validation arm never re-arms, and the queue stalls until a human deletes the label. On 2026-10-17 alone this required 4 manual interventions (3× on fa #1563, 1× on fa #1566) — each one papering over the same defect.

## Why this framing

- **Retracted:** "operator clears stale validation_failed labels" (done 4× on 2026-10-17). Owner directive: manual clearing masks the bug; the pipeline must self-reset. This card fixes the machine, not the symptom.
- **Retracted:** "the SM re-arms on label removal" as the designed reset path. The designed reset is the *head-change event*, per the machine's own published comment contract on parked PRs: *"Your push clears the validation_failed park via the head-change reset."* The contract exists; the implementation is what is broken.

## Architecture

Named lifecycle of the park state (subject of every verb is explicit — the OBJECT being mutated is the **PR's label set**, keyed to a **head SHA**):

```
push event (kicker / rework leg / operator / merge-main)
        │
        ▼
[head-change detector] ──reads──▶ PR.headRefOid (BEFORE vs AFTER)
        │ heads differ
        ▼
[park reset] ──removes──▶ label validation_failed  (only if present)
        │                       │
        │                       └── invariant: label removal is unconditional
        │                           on head change — never re-checks old state
        ▼
[arm gate] ──sees──▶ no park label → PR eligible for validation arm
```

**Invariants (asserted by tests, not prose):**
- **I1** — For every PR, `labelPresent(validation_failed)` ⟹ the label's recorded head SHA == current `headRefOid`. Any mismatch is unreachable state; the reset makes it impossible, not merely unlikely.
- **I2** — The reset fires for EVERY head-mutation source: kicker push, machine rework push, operator push, silent merge-main branch update by the merge bot. No source may bypass the detector.
- **I3** — Reset and removal are idempotent and race-safe: N concurrent head-change events produce exactly ≤1 label removal and never a re-add.
- **I4** — The published comment contract stays true verbatim: any push that changes the head clears the park; no comment edit needed (the contract was right, the code was wrong).

## Capability surface (every head-mutation source → reset obligation)

| Head-mutation source | Resets park today? | Must reset (this card) |
|---|---|---|
| 🥁 kicker push (armed validation refresh) | **NO** (observed: fa #1566, kicker 18:09Z, label persisted 20+ min) | YES — core |
| Machine rework-leg push (fix commit) | unknown, assumed NO (same code path gap) | YES — core |
| Operator push to PR branch | NO (fa #1563 cycle, 3×) | YES — core |
| Merge-bot silent merge-main branch update | unknown | YES — core |
| PR reopened / retargeted | NO (not observed, same class) | YES — second tier |

**Tiered inventory:**
- **Core (this card):** I1–I4 for all four core sources; reset removes the label and leaves an audit trail entry (machine log line `park-reset: <pr> head <old>→<new>`).
- **Second tier (opt-in follow-up):** reset also *re-dispatches* validation automatically for armed-eligible PRs (today a separate SM turn does this — fine to keep).
- **Excluded (rationale):** resetting on *check-run completion* events — completion is not a head change and would fight the label's purpose (the label is the park); excluded deliberately.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — Unit: given a PR carrying `validation_failed` with recorded head `H1`, when the head-change detector observes `headRefOid` becoming `H2 ≠ H1`, the reset removes the label. *Hook: park-state unit test over the detector with injected head refs.*
- **AC2** — Integration (fake GitHub): each of the four core sources produces a head change → exactly one label removal follows within the same SM/merge-bot turn; no removal occurs when head is unchanged. *Hook: scripted scenario runner with recorded API fixtures.*
- **AC3** — Contract: the detector compares full SHAs (not prefixes, not branch names) and treats force-push (same branch, new SHA) identically to fast-forward. *Hook: AC2 variant with force-push fixture.*
- **AC4** — Race: two concurrent pushes (kicker + operator) → ≤1 removal, no error, no re-add. *Hook: concurrent-event fixture.*
- **AC5** — Regression (live-shape): replay the fa #1566 timeline (label set on `H1`, kicker push to `bf0828c4`, all checks green) → label absent at end of the kicker's own run. *Hook: E2E scenario keyed to the recorded run ids (39054011685).*

## Test plan

### Test matrix
- `UT-1..3` — pure state machine of the park lifecycle (set/park/reset), no IO. Maps AC1, AC3, AC4.
- `IT-1..4` — fake-API scenarios, one per head-mutation source. Maps AC2.
- `E2E-1` — real repo sandbox: push red → label set → push green head → label gone without any human call. Maps AC5.
- `REG-1` — fa queue simulation: 5 PRs parked on stale labels under the old behavior replayed against the new code; assert none remain parked after one SM pass. **CI rule: a red REG job blocks merge of this fix even when UT/IT/E2E are all green** (this is exactly the class of bug that only shows up in queue shape).

### Edge / border cases
- **E1** — Head changes while a validation run for the OLD head is still in flight: old run's result must never re-set the park for the new head (result is keyed to the SHA it ran on).
- **E2** — Push that keeps the tree identical (empty amend, re-tag): SHA changes anyway → reset fires (correct: a new SHA is a new claim of "look again").
- **E3** — Label manually re-added between head change and SM turn: the reset has fired already; the label now records the NEW head and behaves as a fresh park (no hidden unbounded loops).
- **E4** — GitHub API failure mid-reset: retry with backoff; the SM turn must not crash; worst case the label survives ONE extra turn (degradation path, not a stall).
- **E5** — PR closed while parked: label irrelevant; no reset needed; no crash on later events.

## Non-goals

- Changing WHAT counts as red (check-selection logic is untouched).
- Auto-dispatching validation on reset (second tier; the existing arm gate handles it).
- Touching `rework-loop-escalated` / `blocked` / `validation_failed`-on-current-head semantics — those are separate state machines (see agents#990 for the escalation one).
- Manual label-clearing runbooks — permanently retired; any future human clear of this label is a bug report, not a procedure.

## Open questions

- **Q1** — Where does the fix land: the shared dma/SM scripts in dmtools-agents (both repos' legs resolve `latest`) or fa-specific config? *Default assumption: agents repo, shared path, since the contract text ships from there.*
- **Q2** — Should the reset emit the audit comment on the PR (visible trail for operators) or only a machine-log line? *Default: machine-log line only; PR comments on automated housekeeping became noise today.*

## References

- Live instances 2026-10-17: fa #1563 (3×), fa #1566 (kicker push run 39054011685, head `bf0828c4`).
- Precedent for machine-bug-fix flow: dmtools-agents#969 (rework retry loop fix shipped through the same pipeline).
- Sibling defect (same family, separate card): dmtools-agents#990 — rework-loop-escalated false positive also jams the validate-armed pointer.
- The contract sentence being violated, quoted from the machine's own parked-PR comment: *"Your push clears the validation_failed park via the head-change reset."*

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write

# gh-994: validation_failed label not auto-cleared on head change (park-reset broken) — operator hit it 4x today

## Description

## Goal — validation_failed park state becomes a pure function of the CURRENT head (v2, full reframe per create-goal discipline)

One sentence: **the `validation_failed` label on a PR always and only reflects the check state of the PR's current head** — any head change resets the park automatically, so no PR can ever sit "parked" on a failure that belongs to a superseded commit.

Today the label is sticky across head changes: after a kicker push / rework push / operator push moves the head, the label set for the OLD head is not removed, the SM keeps treating the PR as parked, the validation arm never re-arms, and the queue stalls until a human deletes the label. On 2026-10-17 alone this required 4 manual interventions (3× on fa #1563, 1× on fa #1566) — each one papering over the same defect.

## Why this framing

- **Retracted:** "operator clears stale validation_failed labels" (done 4× on 2026-10-17). Owner directive: manual clearing masks the bug; the pipeline must self-reset. This card fixes the machine, not the symptom.
- **Retracted:** "the SM re-arms on label removal" as the designed reset path. The designed reset is the *head-change event*, per the machine's own published comment contract on parked PRs: *"Your push clears the validation_failed park via the head-change reset."* The contract exists; the implementation is what is broken.

## Architecture

Named lifecycle of the park state (subject of every verb is explicit — the OBJECT being mutated is the **PR's label set**, keyed to a **head SHA**):

```
push event (kicker / rework leg / operator / merge-main)
        │
        ▼
[head-change detector] ──reads──▶ PR.headRefOid (BEFORE vs AFTER)
        │ heads differ
        ▼
[park reset] ──removes──▶ label validation_failed  (only if present)
        │                       │
        │                       └── invariant: label removal is unconditional
        │                           on head change — never re-checks old state
        ▼
[arm gate] ──sees──▶ no park label → PR eligible for validation arm
```

**Invariants (asserted by tests, not prose):**
- **I1** — For every PR, `labelPresent(validation_failed)` ⟹ the label's recorded head SHA == current `headRefOid`. Any mismatch is unreachable state; the reset makes it impossible, not merely unlikely.
- **I2** — The reset fires for EVERY head-mutation source: kicker push, machine rework push, operator push, silent merge-main branch update by the merge bot. No source may bypass the detector.
- **I3** — Reset and removal are idempotent and race-safe: N concurrent head-change events produce exactly ≤1 label removal and never a re-add.
- **I4** — The published comment contract stays true verbatim: any push that changes the head clears the park; no comment edit needed (the contract was right, the code was wrong).

## Capability surface (every head-mutation source → reset obligation)

| Head-mutation source | Resets park today? | Must reset (this card) |
|---|---|---|
| 🥁 kicker push (armed validation refresh) | **NO** (observed: fa #1566, kicker 18:09Z, label persisted 20+ min) | YES — core |
| Machine rework-leg push (fix commit) | unknown, assumed NO (same code path gap) | YES — core |
| Operator push to PR branch | NO (fa #1563 cycle, 3×) | YES — core |
| Merge-bot silent merge-main branch update | unknown | YES — core |
| PR reopened / retargeted | NO (not observed, same class) | YES — second tier |

**Tiered inventory:**
- **Core (this card):** I1–I4 for all four core sources; reset removes the label and leaves an audit trail entry (machine log line `park-reset: <pr> head <old>→<new>`).
- **Second tier (opt-in follow-up):** reset also *re-dispatches* validation automatically for armed-eligible PRs (today a separate SM turn does this — fine to keep).
- **Excluded (rationale):** resetting on *check-run completion* events — completion is not a head change and would fight the label's purpose (the label is the park); excluded deliberately.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — Unit: given a PR carrying `validation_failed` with recorded head `H1`, when the head-change detector observes `headRefOid` becoming `H2 ≠ H1`, the reset removes the label. *Hook: park-state unit test over the detector with injected head refs.*
- **AC2** — Integration (fake GitHub): each of the four core sources produces a head change → exactly one label removal follows within the same SM/merge-bot turn; no removal occurs when head is unchanged. *Hook: scripted scenario runner with recorded API fixtures.*
- **AC3** — Contract: the detector compares full SHAs (not prefixes, not branch names) and treats force-push (same branch, new SHA) identically to fast-forward. *Hook: AC2 variant with force-push fixture.*
- **AC4** — Race: two concurrent pushes (kicker + operator) → ≤1 removal, no error, no re-add. *Hook: concurrent-event fixture.*
- **AC5** — Regression (live-shape): replay the fa #1566 timeline (label set on `H1`, kicker push to `bf0828c4`, all checks green) → label absent at end of the kicker's own run. *Hook: E2E scenario keyed to the recorded run ids (39054011685).*

## Test plan

### Test matrix
- `UT-1..3` — pure state machine of the park lifecycle (set/park/reset), no IO. Maps AC1, AC3, AC4.
- `IT-1..4` — fake-API scenarios, one per head-mutation source. Maps AC2.
- `E2E-1` — real repo sandbox: push red → label set → push green head → label gone without any human call. Maps AC5.
- `REG-1` — fa queue simulation: 5 PRs parked on stale labels under the old behavior replayed against the new code; assert none remain parked after one SM pass. **CI rule: a red REG job blocks merge of this fix even when UT/IT/E2E are all green** (this is exactly the class of bug that only shows up in queue shape).

### Edge / border cases
- **E1** — Head changes while a validation run for the OLD head is still in flight: old run's result must never re-set the park for the new head (result is keyed to the SHA it ran on).
- **E2** — Push that keeps the tree identical (empty amend, re-tag): SHA changes anyway → reset fires (correct: a new SHA is a new claim of "look again").
- **E3** — Label manually re-added between head change and SM turn: the reset has fired already; the label now records the NEW head and behaves as a fresh park (no hidden unbounded loops).
- **E4** — GitHub API failure mid-reset: retry with backoff; the SM turn must not crash; worst case the label survives ONE extra turn (degradation path, not a stall).
- **E5** — PR closed while parked: label irrelevant; no reset needed; no crash on later events.

## Non-goals

- Changing WHAT counts as red (check-selection logic is untouched).
- Auto-dispatching validation on reset (second tier; the existing arm gate handles it).
- Touching `rework-loop-escalated` / `blocked` / `validation_failed`-on-current-head semantics — those are separate state machines (see agents#990 for the escalation one).
- Manual label-clearing runbooks — permanently retired; any future human clear of this label is a bug report, not a procedure.

## Open questions

- **Q1** — Where does the fix land: the shared dma/SM scripts in dmtools-agents (both repos' legs resolve `latest`) or fa-specific config? *Default assumption: agents repo, shared path, since the contract text ships from there.*
- **Q2** — Should the reset emit the audit comment on the PR (visible trail for operators) or only a machine-log line? *Default: machine-log line only; PR comments on automated housekeeping became noise today.*

## References

- Live instances 2026-10-17: fa #1563 (3×), fa #1566 (kicker push run 39054011685, head `bf0828c4`).
- Precedent for machine-bug-fix flow: dmtools-agents#969 (rework retry loop fix shipped through the same pipeline).
- Sibling defect (same family, separate card): dmtools-agents#990 — rework-loop-escalated false positive also jams the validate-armed pointer.
